messages:
Samir: Heads up — seeing a P99 spike for cohort `edge-eu` after runtime v2.14 rolled through canary ~2h ago. P50 unchanged, P95 up ~1.1x, P99 ~3.2x baseline. dashboard: https://redwood/d/latency/edge-eu
Jessica: ugh. can you paste the query/time window? any recent config or kernel selector flips?
Samir: window 13:30-15:10 UTC. Query: `latency.p99{service:runtime,cohort:edge-eu}.rollup(1m)` Also note a small uptick in auth token latency around same time.
Kyle: is this returning 429s or just slow 200s? any error budget burns?
Samir: mostly 200s but long tail. No 429s. Auth token fetch p99 went from 180ms -> 2.8s.
Nina: did the canary include the new kernel heuristic for small batch FP16 (`kernel.pref_fp16=true`)?
Marco: yes — that heuristic shipped with v2.14 canary. It was intended to reduce latency on long sequences but changed the kernel selection path.
Lisa: ops-bot, create incident and attach current graphs?
ops-bot: INCIDENT-1142 created: "canary cohort edge-eu p99 regression" — paging oncall. Links: https://redwood/incident/1142
Jessica: quick repro: can you run a synthetic trace with seq_len=64, batch=1 against canary instances and collect nvprof / compile times?
Samir: running now. snippet from the slow trace: ```
[2026-03-17T14:47:12Z] nv_jit_compile: 120ms
[2026-03-17T14:47:12Z] kernel_swap_eviction: 950ms
[2026-03-17T14:47:12Z] forward: 1800ms
```
Kyle: kernel_swap_eviction at ~1s is suspicious — indicates frequent JIT/evict churn for small sequences. That's consistent with a new selector picking heavier kernels.
Nina: any change to KV cache keying or warming during rollout? Could be cache churn + compile = tail.
Marco: no KV key changes. But the kernel path now keeps larger scratch buffers which can cause eviction on smaller GPUs that we used in edge-eu pool.
Lisa: immediate mitigation: can we traffic-split 80/20 back to previous runtime version for edge-eu (keep 20% on v2.14) and enable kernel selector gate off for the canary pods?
Samir: starting 80/20 split now. ops-bot: run traffic-split command.
ops-bot: traffic-split executed: edge-eu -> {v2.13:80%, v2.14:20%}.
Jessica: also propose a config toggle to disable `prefer_fp16` for instances with <24GB mem — that should avoid the eviction path.
Marco: I can patch the selector gate in 10m and roll to the canary group B after we validate. Plan: (1) split traffic, (2) gate selector on canary, (3) run synthetic probe for 30m, (4) bisect if still high.
Kyle: bisect idea: turn off kernel flag in half of v2.14 backends (A vs B) to get a clean A/B signal rather than full rollback. If p99 falls in the off group that's strong evidence.
Samir: launching bisect now: toggling selector=false for subset A (10% of traffic).
ops-bot: rollout patch started -> service/runtime/canary-a selector=false (10% traffic).
Samir: early numbers: after traffic-split P99 dropped ~40% overall; the 10% cohort with selector=false already shows P99 ~baseline.
Nina: that matches hypothesis: selector produced extra JIT/eviction churn on small-memory edge hosts.
Marco: root-cause hypothesis: `prefer_fp16` heuristic picks FP16 kernels that allocate larger scratch buffers on some GPU types; combined with tighter packing in edge-eu leads to eviction + JIT compile thrash. Tail appears only for short sequences (seq<=128).
Jessica: next steps: 1) keep split at 80/20 for 1h, 2) revert selector default to false for pools with <24GB, 3) prepare a proper kernel footprint check in selector to prevent allocations beyond threshold, 4) run a full canary with synthetic short-seq workload.
Lisa: I'll notify customer-success for any high-touch tenants in edge-eu and open a retro note. Also adding a temporary pricing credit for impacted requests? (cc @billing)
Samir: thanks. I'll update INCIDENT-1142 with logs, perf counters (nvtx, iowait, compile counts) and the bisect result. If P99 doesn't return to baseline after 1h we'll roll v2.14 fully back for edge-eu.
Kyle: FYI, collect `dmesg` / OOM logs too — if scratch buffers push some pods into OOM it's important.
Marco: working on a small runtime patch to avoid selecting FP16 when projected scratch > 30% GPU memory. Will submit PR and request fast-track review.
Samir: great. thumbs up if you want me to keep this thread updated every 15m :thumbsup:
Jessica: please do. add brief SLA impact estimate in the incident doc.
Lisa: noted. I'll ping support queue with a short blurb for customers.
Samir: updating — will check back in 15m with updated p99 numbers.
